subject: Compliance packaging: amortize implementation vs monthly pass-through for KMS/HSM & audit logs
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@healthgrid.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on compliance line items and options

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked solid. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of pricing clarifications before we run this up the chain:

1) For the KMS/HSM requirement, do you invoice seats monthly as a recurring charge, or is there an option to amortize/setup as a one-time implementation fee with a lower ongoing charge?
2) Audit logs: we need 7 years retention for certain workflows. Do you have retention tiers (90/365/7yrs) and how are those priced (per GB/month vs flat tier)?
3) Data residency: we will need US-only residency for PHI. Is that a separate line item, and can that be combined with KMS/HSM as a bundled discount?

We expect to push a PO in the next 4–6 weeks but want to lock the preferred commercial structure now. If you could send a short note with two concrete packaging options (pass-through recurring vs amortized implementation + reduced recurring) and a sample SOW, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it,
Elena
---
Elena Torres
Director, Security & Compliance
HealthGrid
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@healthgrid.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on compliance line items and options

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Below are two pragmatic packaging paths we typically offer for HIPAA/HSM/residency combos; I included approximate commercial examples (ballpark) so procurement can model them. I attached a short worksheet and a draft SOW to this thread.

Option 1 — Pass-through / recurring (simpler accounting):
- Residency (US-only): $12k/month
- Audit log retention: Tiered pricing; 90 days included, 365 days + $1.20/GB/month, 7yr retention quoted at $0.60/GB/month for long-term cold storage (example).
- HSM seats: $1,800/seat/month (operational seat + maintenance)
- No upfront implementation fee aside from standard deployment support (billed as time & materials)
- Pros: predictable monthly line items, easier for ops.

Option 2 — Amortized implementation + reduced recurring (preferred for capex-style buyers):
- One-time implementation/amortization: $210k (covers HSM provisioning, residency setup, audit pipeline work) amortized over 24 months in our pricing model (effectively $8,750/month for year 1 in ARR math)
- Recurring residency fee reduced to $6k/month (discounted because initial infra paid up front)
- HSM seats reduced to $1,000/seat/month when amortized fee accepted
- Audit log retention tiers: same unit pricing but we can include a 12% credit on storage costs year 1 if you accept amortization
- Pros: lower recurring OPEX, easier to justify consolidation of one-time infra set up into project budget

Suggested incentive for a 12-month committed term: 10% credit on recurring fees year 1 (or we can do a one-time $25k implementation credit if you close by June 15).

Next steps I suggest:
- I updated the attached worksheet (20270530-compliance-pricing-worksheet.xlsx) with the two scenarios and sample calculations for your expected throughput (I used the numbers you gave in the demo).
- If you prefer Option 2 I can draft a short SOW and a PO routing checklist (SOW attached).

Notes on accounting/ordering: long-term retention can be met via cheaper archival storage with monthly tiering; we can map to your internal GL codes if Procurement sends them along.

If helpful, Ben can chime on the accounting/crediting side (cc'd). Soojin is on the thread for the HSM/crypto questions.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: 20270530-compliance-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (xlsx); SOW-draft-HealthGrid.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-30T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on compliance line items and options

Mateo — quick note from finance: if we go with the amortized implementation route, accounting prefers a 24-month amortization window for the one-time fee to match revenue recognition; that keeps the recurring charge simple on the ledger. For commercial flexibility, offering a 25% first-year credit on storage costs (or the $25k implementation credit you suggested) is fine — recommend we lean to the fixed credit (easier to model for procurement).

Also suggest we place a clear PO acceptance deadline on the quote (we noted June 15 above). If Procurement agrees, we can include a short clause in the SOW calling out credit application and invoice schedule.

Ben
VP, Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena@healthgrid.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: 2027-06-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on compliance line items and options

Mateo — thanks, this is helpful. HealthGrid prefers the amortized implementation approach (Option 2) to keep ongoing operating costs down. The $25k implementation credit if we sign by June 15 sounds reasonable — we will try to hit that window.

Could you:
- Send an updated SOW that reflects the 24-month amortization and the $25k credit applied to the implementation line;
- Include a short PO instructions doc (who to send the PO to, invoice cadence, and remittance details).

I attached a brief PO checklist from Procurement — they asked for the routing and remittance info before issuing the PO. Once we have the SOW and PO instructions we can circulate internally and aim to send a PO within the two-week window.

Best,
Elena
